system_overview: This specification models a binary search algorithm for finding an item in a sorted sequence of integers. It is one of the examples from Section 7.3 of 'Proving Safety Properties' by Leslie Lamport. The module defines the algorithm using PlusCal, provides the translated state-machine specification, and includes a complete machine-checked proof of its partial correctness (safety) property. The algorithm takes a sorted sequence and a target value, and returns either the index of the target in the sequence or zero if the target is not present.
actors_and_components: The system is a single sequential algorithm. There is one actor: the search procedure, which iterates over a sorted sequence to locate a target value. No concurrency or multiple processes are involved.
state_variables: The system maintains: (1) a sorted sequence of integers drawn from a specified set of integer values, (2) a target value to search for, (3) a lower bound index for the current search range, (4) an upper bound index for the current search range, (5) an output index (zero if the target has not been found, or the position of the target when found), and (6) a program counter tracking whether the algorithm is still running or has terminated.
initial_state: The sorted sequence is chosen nondeterministically from the set of all sorted sequences over the specified value set. The target value is chosen nondeterministically from the value set. The lower bound is set to 1 (the start of the sequence). The upper bound is set to the length of the sequence. The output index is set to 0 (not found). The program counter is set to the main loop label.
actions: The algorithm has one main action corresponding to one iteration of the binary search loop: (1) If the lower bound does not exceed the upper bound and the output is still zero, compute the midpoint of the current range and retrieve the value at that position. If the midpoint value equals the target, set the output to the midpoint index. If the target is less than the midpoint value, move the upper bound to one below the midpoint. Otherwise, move the lower bound to one above the midpoint. (2) If the loop condition is no longer satisfied (lower bound exceeds upper bound, or a result has been found), the algorithm terminates. A stuttering step is also included to prevent deadlock after termination.
safety_properties: Partial correctness: when the algorithm terminates, if the target value exists somewhere in the sorted sequence, then the output index points to a position containing the target value; if the target does not exist in the sequence, the output index is zero. An inductive invariant is defined that strengthens this postcondition to be preserved across all transitions.
liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches its terminal state. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
model_bounds: The set of allowed integer values is declared as a constant that must be a subset of the integers. For model checking, a companion module redefines the sequence operator to produce only sequences up to a bounded length.
additional_assumptions: The set of values is assumed to be a subset of the integers. The sorted sequences are defined as those sequences over the value set where elements are in non-decreasing order. The specification includes a complete machine-checked safety proof using the TLAPS proof system, which verifies that the inductive invariant implies the correctness postcondition.
